title: SYSK Live Christmas Spectacular!
summary: Live Christmas spectacular recorded at the Center Stage Theater in Atlanta, Georgia, with Josh and Chuck. The episode covers the history of aluminum Christmas trees (Aluminum Specialties of Manitowoc, Wisconsin, and copycat makers, and the Charlie Brown Christmas Special link), three Christmas miracle stories (the 1852 hat box baby in Arizona, the 1950 Meredith Victory evacuation from Hungnam, Korea, and Daisy the rat terrier found in Knoxville at Christmas 2006), the Teddy Ruxpin talking bear of 1985, European Christmas monsters (Yule Cat, Frau Perchta, Belsnickel, Hans Trapp, Père Fouettard), and how to make a hot toddy. It closes with the history of Christmas ghost stories and a read-aloud of Alan Silverberg's Hanukkah book Meet the Latkes, followed by a group carol.

segments.title: Live show opening and book plug
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the live Christmas show at the Center Stage Theater in Atlanta, mention visual cues posted on Facebook, and plug the Hanukkah book Meet the Latkes by Alan Silverberg.

segments.title: History of the aluminum Christmas tree
segments.summary: Aluminum Specialties of Manitowoc, Wisconsin, made affordable aluminum trees after seeing a pricier one in Chicago. Tire salesmen sold them in Wisconsin, many copycat brands followed, and the trees fell out of fashion, with Charlie Brown often blamed.

segments.title: Three Christmas miracles
segments.summary: Three stories: the 1852 hat box baby found near Superior, Arizona, and adopted in the 1930s by a couple who named her Sharon; the 1950 evacuation of about 14,000 Korean civilians from Hungnam on the SS Meredith Victory, with no deaths and five births; and Daisy the rat terrier, found in Knoxville, Tennessee, after going missing from Aurora, Colorado, in 2006.

segments.title: Teddy Ruxpin talking bear
segments.summary: History of the Teddy Ruxpin talking toy bear, created by Disney imagineer Ken Forcey. It used a cassette and radio signals to animate its face, sold out quickly in 1985, got ABC specials, and spawned imitators.

segments.title: European Christmas monsters
segments.summary: Overview of frightening European Christmas figures: the Yule Cat of Iceland, Frau Perchta of Germany and Austria, Belsnickel of German and Pennsylvania Dutch tradition, Hans Trapp, and Père Fouettard in France, who was made to work for St. Nick.

segments.title: How to make a hot toddy
segments.summary: Josh demonstrates a hot toddy with rye whiskey, honey, lemon, and hot water, and discusses its possible origins (Todd's Well in Edinburgh, Dr. Robert Todd, Indian toddy) and health claims.

segments.title: Christmas ghost stories tradition
segments.summary: Explains the winter solstice roots of Christmas ghost stories, the Victorian English tradition described by Jerome K. Jerome, and why ghosts appear in A Christmas Carol.

segments.title: Reading: Meet the Latkes
segments.summary: The hosts read Alan Silverberg's children's book Meet the Latkes, which tells the story of Hanukkah through the Latke family, including the Maccabees and the oil miracle.

segments.title: Group carol and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts lead the audience in a Christmas carol and wish listeners happy holidays.
